name: PC817
description: Single-channel optocoupler: an infrared LED optically coupled to a phototransistor, giving galvanic isolation between input and output. Ubiquitous for mains/secondary feedback in SMPS, microcontroller input isolation, and level translation across ground domains.

DIP-4.notes: pin 1 marked with a dot/chamfer. Input LED on pins 1-2, output transistor on pins 3-4.

typical_application: Drive the input LED through a series resistor (sized for ~10mA) from the isolated source; the phototransistor on the output side conducts proportionally. Standard secondary-to-primary feedback path in switching supplies (often paired with a TL431).
gotchas: current transfer ratio (CTR) varies enormously by grade (suffix) and drops with age and temperature; design with margin
slow: bandwidth is only tens of kHz, not for fast data (use a logic-gate optocoupler for that)
the LED has a forward voltage like any LED; size the series resistor for the input supply
respect the isolation barrier on the PCB layout; do not run traces under the package between sides
